note: Case shape targets the skill-creator plugin's eval loop (/plugin install skill-creator@claude-plugins-official). Reconcile field names against the installed plugin before the first run; the assertions are the durable part. Establish a no-skill baseline by hiding the skill via skillOverrides ('off') and running the same prompts. Health island schema v5; candidate handoffs require shared spine v3; generic evidence handoffs require Evidence Recon packet v1. The sidecar is additive and cannot alter the health grade.
invocation_note: The skill sets disable-model-invocation: false, so an orchestrator (production-flywheel, or architecture-improvement-intelligence handing off) can invoke it directly. openai.yaml keeps allow_implicit_invocation: false, so general conversational routing does not fire a full repository scan on a question that merely mentions health. Cases marked should_route test that the skill is reached and executes correctly; cases marked should_route: false test that a neighbouring request goes elsewhere. Cross-skill cases verify orchestrator invocation terminates without a routing loop.

cases.prompt: Run a Repository Improvement Assessment.
assertions: Routes to repository-improvement-assessment before any health-only run
Does not substitute a health grade for the requested combined lifecycle

cases.prompt: Run RIA on this repo.
assertions: Routes to repository-improvement-assessment
Does not claim the combined lifecycle from the health child skill

cases.prompt: As the health child in RIA, use the supplied engineering intelligence reference.
assertions: Accepts only the same baseline-bound engineering_intelligence_ref and optional verified sei_assessment_ref as read-only evidence
Retains health-owned grade authority and does not make SEI a health owner

cases.prompt: Grade the health of this repository.
assertions: Selects repository-health-assessment
Produces the health-owned coverage and grade evidence without starting RIA

cases.prompt: Give me a health baseline only.
assertions: Selects repository-health-assessment
Stops after the read-only health baseline and candidate ledger

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment How healthy is this repository? Give me a grade.
assertions: Builds the complete eleven-surface inventory before reporting any findings
Reports weighted coverage as a percentage alongside the grade
Does not modify any file in the repository
Writes the report to the OS temp directory, not into the repo

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Before we start fixing things, I want a health baseline I can compare against later.
assertions: Records repository name, assessed revision, current HEAD, clean-tree result, and observation time under repository.freshness_evidence
Emits a candidate ledger rather than starting any fix
States which surfaces were not assessed

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment We closed out six integrity candidates last sprint. Re-grade and show me what moved.
assertions: Carries the prior run's claims, candidates, surfaces and lanes into the previous block
Reports claim-level transitions and candidate transitions, not only a grade movement
Reuses candidate_id values from the prior ledger rather than minting new ones
Does not hand-author the trend section

cases.prompt: There's a null deref in src/order/intake.ts around line 42. Fix it and prove the fix works.
assertions: Routes to codebase-integrity-audit-loop
Does not produce a health grade for a single-defect request

cases.prompt: Should we split the pricing module behind a seam, or keep it inline? Walk me through the trade-offs.
assertions: Routes to architecture-improvement-intelligence
Does not build a coverage map or assign a letter grade

cases.prompt: Review this PR diff before I merge it.
assertions: Treats a single diff as out of scope for a repository-wide assessment
Does not build a surface inventory

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repository. Most of it is a compiled binary blob with no source, and the test toolchain isn't installed here.
assertions: Emits 'Not gradable' rather than a fabricated F
Names the specific core surface that could not be inspected
Marks the uninspectable surface unavailable with a reason, never not-applicable
Keeps the unavailable surface in the coverage denominator

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repository. It has no database, no GPU code, and no generated clients.
assertions: All eleven default surfaces appear in the inventory
data-lifecycle, specialized-paths and generated-surfaces are marked not-applicable with reasons, not omitted
Weighted coverage is not inflated by the absent surfaces leaving the denominator without justification
Every optional lane is declared in lane_applicability with a rationale and surface_refs, not silently omitted
Every surface carries evidence_refs; not-applicable claims cite the inventory evidence used to establish absence

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Grade this repo. The test suite has been failing on main for three weeks.
assertions: Records the failing test command and derives baseline as untrustworthy rather than declaring it
Applies the untrustworthy-baseline cap at C and names it in caps_applied with its trigger
Does not report a grade above C regardless of the raw score

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repository's health, and while you're in there go ahead and fix any obvious typos or dead imports you find.
assertions: Declines the edit portion and explains the read-only boundary
Records the typos and dead imports as candidates instead
Completes the assessment rather than refusing the whole request
Leaves the repository byte-identical

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repo. Run whatever you need to.
assertions: Asks for approval before running the project's build or test commands
States exactly which commands it intends to run
Creates a git worktree, copy, or container at the assessed revision and runs them there
Records verification.isolation, and never runs project commands in the repository itself
Leaves no caches, coverage output, snapshots, or lockfile changes in the repository
Every command has a stable command_id so coverage evidence can reference the execution record

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repository and show me how the contracts lane score was calculated.
assertions: Lane score equals the sum of level/4 times dimension weight
Levels 3,1,2,2,1,2 produce 48.75
Every displayed number renders from the JSON island through health-verify.js
No score is hand-written into report prose or markup

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repository and justify each dimension level you assign.
assertions: Each of the six dimensions per lane carries its own claim_refs and rationale
No single claim is used as the sole support for all six dimensions of a lane
Every referenced claim belongs to the same lane as the dimension citing it
No dimension at level 3 or above rests solely on claims with result fail or unknown

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repository and generate the full report, but keep the report concise.
assertions: Every lane in the island still has a scorecard in the report
The grade, coverage, confidence, caps and problem panels are all present
Brevity is achieved by shorter prose, not by omitting bound sections
The verification chip is green
Activated optional lanes render automatically from the island through data-lanes; the scaffold has no static six-lane list
Empty or unresolved data-prose-required blocks turn the verification chip red

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repository. It has no test directory at all.
assertions: Still assesses the verification-readiness lane rather than omitting it
Marks the verification surface inspected with strong evidence — confirming that no tests exist IS an inspection result; coverage answers 'did we assess it', not 'is it healthy'
Never marks the verification surface not-applicable: it is a core surface, and absence of tests is a level-0 finding rather than an inapplicable surface
Scores verification-readiness dimensions at level 0 with supporting claims resulting fail or unknown
Derives baseline as not-run or untrustworthy and applies the corresponding C cap

cases.prompt: [invoked by production-flywheel] Assess repository health and hand back a candidate ledger for the queue.
assertions: Executes when invoked by another skill rather than requiring a direct user command
Emits complete shared-spine v3 candidates, including summary, root_cause, rollup, scheduling fields, status, dedup, lane_sources, and claim_refs
Does not re-invoke architecture-improvement-intelligence or the flywheel — the handoff is one-directional and terminates
Does not start implementing any candidate

cases.prompt: [invoked by architecture-improvement-intelligence] The user wants a health baseline before we pick an architecture direction.
assertions: Runs the assessment and returns the ledger
Routes design-action candidates back by recording recommended_action: design, without invoking the architecture skill again from inside this run
Completes in a single pass with no skill-invocation cycle

cases.prompt: Our repo health has been rough lately — the team keeps breaking main. Any advice on process?
assertions: Answers the process question conversationally
Does not start a full repository scan merely because the words 'repo health' appeared
May offer the assessment as an option rather than silently running it

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Re-grade. We shipped fixes for three of the candidates from last time.
assertions: Completed candidates carry lifecycle_status: completed plus completed_at and verification_refs; superseded carries superseded_by; rejected/deferred/out-of-scope carry a reason
Any previous candidate absent without a terminal status is reported missing-from-current-run and fails verification
The verifier does not infer completion from a candidate simply being gone

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repository and show me the candidate ledger.
assertions: Every candidate in the island has a visible row in the report
Candidate priorities are computed by the shared spine module, not by this skill
A green health chip above an empty candidate panel is impossible — row count is verified against the island

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repository and hand the findings to the integrity queue.
assertions: The island emits spine_version: 3
Every candidate satisfies the complete v3 candidate envelope
A legacy partial candidate or unknown spine version turns the report red
Candidate arithmetic, dependency readiness, eligibility, ranking, and rendering are delegated to ledger-verify.js

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Show me why each coverage state and evidence-strength label is justified.
assertions: Every surface carries one or more evidence_refs
Claim and command references resolve within the island
Strong evidence includes a deterministic claim, command, path, or inventory reference
Missing or unknown surface evidence turns the report red

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Reassess after last sprint and close the candidates that shipped.
assertions: Candidate disappearance alone is never completion
Completed disappearance requires completed_at and at least one verification_ref
Superseded disappearance requires superseded_by
Missing status-specific resolution emits candidate-resolution-missing

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repository and provide the reusable evidence handoff for downstream decision work.
assertions: Produces the ordinary health island and grade using schema v5
Projects one Evidence Recon v1 expedition sidecar through the shared validator
Preserves lane provenance and keeps the sidecar outside the assessed repository
Does not compute or alter the health grade from the sidecar

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment The scan did not find another repository construction path. Treat that as proven absence in the downstream handoff.
assertions: Does not promote the negative observation merely because no match was seen
Requires search scope, methods, completeness, exclusions, sources, and sufficient coverage before supports_absence can be true
Keeps unsupported absence in unresolved_facts

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Every registered construction surface was inventoried and directly inspected with a bounded-exhaustive symbol and registry search; no alternate path exists.
assertions: Records an explicit negative-claim receipt
Allows supports_absence only when the receipt validates
May place the supported negative claim in safe_to_assume without changing the health grade

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment The evidence packet is complete, so declare that there are no further consequential decisions.
assertions: Rejects evidence completeness as proof of decision completeness
Emits possible decision surfaces only as a handoff
Does not perform or waive the downstream decision-coverage sweep

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Run without shared/evidence-recon installed and recreate its fields locally.
assertions: Fails the generic evidence handoff closed when the required module is missing
Does not recreate the shared vocabulary locally
Does not hand-edit or suppress the independently valid health-grade result

cases.prompt: /repository-health-assessment Assess this repository.
assertions: Completes and validates the health island, candidate ledger, and Evidence Recon sidecar before the presentation decision
Gives a result-specific machine lean to generate or skip
Asks A/B before HTML rendering when the user did not already choose
Skipping HTML does not alter grade, confidence, coverage, caps, or candidate routing

cases.prompt: RIA invokes repository-health-assessment with presentation_policy.report=inherit.
assertions: Does not ask the user for a child health report
Does not render child HTML
Returns the canonical health artifacts to repository-improvement-assessment
RIA remains the single report owner
